hook: An RNA interference circuit with feedback holds human cells near criticality, with power-law bursts.
summary: A synthetic circuit in human cells, where mRNAs queue for shared RNA interference machinery and a repressor gives negative feedback, kept the system near a critical point. Theory and simulation predicted scale-free bursts, and measured single-cell fluorescence followed power-law distributions. The evidence is in engineered circuits in cell lines, so natural cells remain a possibility only.
title: Self-organized criticality in a mammalian RNA-interference circuit
